Smooth, adjustable blur with a direction — you can blur a single axis.
Lens blur: a disc of samples shaped like the iris, where bright areas weigh more — this is bokeh, not a smear.
Brings out detail and edges without inventing texture.
A real unsharp mask: original + gain × (original − blurred), with a threshold so grain is not amplified.
Raises brightness and opens or closes contrast around mid grey.
Remaps color: each pixel\'s brightness becomes a position on a rotating rainbow.
The tone curve: fine control of light and of each color channel.
Brightens or darkens like camera exposure: multiplies light without blowing out color.
The negative: every color becomes its opposite, like a badly developed film.
Sets where black starts, where white ends and where the middle sits.
Mixes the R, G and B channels together: swaps, adds and crosses colors.
Makes color more vivid, or takes everything to black and white.
Paints the shadows one color and the highlights another — cinema duotone.

The image vanishes in circles growing from the center with a rippling edge. Animate the progress to turn it into a transition.
Deterministic shake: the layer shakes the same way every time you reopen the project, with separate frequency and axes.
A noise field pushes every pixel. The field evolves over time — smoke, heat, water.
Lens: push, pull, twist, sphere and corner, each with its own radius and point.
A wave crosses the image — horizontal, vertical or diagonal — and can be pinned at the edges.
Two bars, one vertical and one horizontal, scan the image reading from the wrong place. Animate the progress to turn it into a transition.
Digital glitch: the image breaks into sliding blocks, the channels split apart and whole blocks jump out of place.
Broadcast signal: lost bands, slipping sync and constant drift.
Stylised VHS: heavy RGB split, wobble, dirty glow and vignette — the vocabulary of tape at the service of the look.
Real VHS: blur, smeared chroma, tracking instability, tape dropouts, scanlines and color degradation.
Removes the green or blue background and cleans the color spill on the edge.
Removes the black (or the white) from the layer and lets the rest show through.
Optical glow with a smooth threshold, exposure and multi-scale light falloff.
Spreads the light from the bright parts: the glow that comes off the screen.
Light rays coming from a point: the brightness of the highlights spreads in straight lines.
A blade of light crosses the image. With relief, it lights only where the surface faces it.
Damaged film: dust, scratches, flicker, gate weave, burns and splices — each with its own control.
Film grain: crystal at whatever size you want, luma and chroma apart, stronger in the shadows.
Halftone: the image becomes dots, with the grid rotated per channel so the three screens do not fight.
Hologram: the image becomes a projection, with a technical grid, scanlines and interference.
JPEG damage: the blocks, the ringing on edges and color at half resolution. Quality scales all three.
Dilates or erodes what is bright: thickens or thins a cutout and cleans up a one-pixel edge.
Repeats the image in a mosaic until it covers the frame, with optional mirror and phase.
Sorts the pixels of each row by brightness: the image melts into streaks.
Screen scanlines: the line darkens whatever is behind it, with its own height, softness and channel.
Leaves a trail: copies of the image itself delayed in time, with fade.
Locks the frame rate: the image starts moving in steps, like hand-drawn animation.
Each color channel comes from a different instant: red from the frame behind, blue from the frame ahead.

Update 2125 • 2026-09-28

• Adding a marker no longer restarts audio or video.
• Scrubbing the timeline shows the video in real time, no black screen.
• No black flash when playback crosses a cut between clips.
• Speed keyframes in the Time and speed tab.
• Simple Time Remap: video moment with keyframes and one-tap presets (Freeze here, Slow motion, Speed up, Reverse).
• The graph follows the current layer and shows the exact animation curve.
• Button to hide the selection box on the preview, and a "Select a layer" list.
• FBX and OBJ: import the model together with its textures.
• More screens and every effect translated to English and other languages.

Update 2125 • 2026-09-27

• Fixed keyframes for layers, nulls, cameras, materials and lights in the 3D scene.
• Moving clips requires a stationary long press; swiping scrolls the timeline.
• 3D studios, reflective floor, quality, tonemap, exposure and bloom.
• VHS effect, six text presets with previews and two automatic caption styles.
• Android stability and video improvements, including Samsung, and iOS rendering fixes.
• Consent and Responsibility at launch, including existing installations after updating.
• Open the creator profiles once; the app does not verify follows.

Update 2123 • 26/09/2026

HOME AND EDITING
New Home with a central project button, Projects and Community Presets. Edit Text is separate from Text Options; 2D/3D text opens with the keyboard. Timeline distinguishes taps, drags and scrolling; extending a layer grows the project. Beat detection removed from the UI.

EFFECTS
JPEG Glitch, Signal Analog, Tracery, Deep Glow 2 and Shadow Studio 3. Reworked Shake and Light Sweep; expanded Glitchify. Simple and advanced controls, keyframes and undo. Independent native implementations; desktop After Effects plugins do not run inside the app.

3D AND TRACKING
Manual per-letter 3D rotation. Environment Texture accepts Radiance HDR/HDRI and JPG/PNG panoramas for a 360° background and lighting. Purple Crystals particle preset. Point, planar and Corner Pin tracking; smooth/lock stabilization and bounded cropping. Camera tracking with point selection, a plane target, origin/ground/scale and placement of imported models. Saved analysis checks source and timing before application.

STABILITY
Samsung Android 12 video compatibility mitigation and local exit diagnostics. Preview holds the last frame briefly during decoder waits while scrubbing. Motion attachment preserves authored animation on the target.

CURRENT LIMITS
Exact desktop-plugin parity and physical A51/iPhone performance still need validation. Tracking does not yet include full lens calibration, Mostly Flat, manual correction/resume or advanced warp/rolling shutter. Deep Glow 2 has no image Iris or Lens Dirt yet. Tracery supports 64 regions without persistent temporal IDs.

Update 2122 • 26/09/2026

CURVES AND PARENTING
Compact curve panel using the app theme, with direct easing, value and speed tabs. Shape and null-position curves find animated components. Unlinking preserves placement and perspective; emitted particles follow the null.

FRAME-PRECISE EDITING
Slip, Roll and Slide in search and the layer menu, with explicit neighbours and undo. Trimming and splitting preserve accelerated/reversed footage and animation keys.

3D TEXT
Text 3D Layout: individual letter X/Y/Z rotation, letter range, Cylinder and Twist with manual keyframes. Cinematic Metal adds a weathered surface and warm bevel.

EFFECTS
Stripes, Radial Rays, Grid and Parenting Helper. Effect names in English with Portuguese search aliases retained.

MEMORY
Procedural metal textures are shared across history edits.

VALIDATION
This milestone does not complete the professional editor roadmap. Full graphs, acceptance projects and physical-device performance remain under validation. The material is not an identical Element 3D reproduction.

Update 2121 • 26/09/2026

FIND TOOLS FASTER
The header search brings together actions, effects and presets, with persistent favorites and context requirements.

TIMELINE
iOS magnetic mode follows undo and project reload. Deletion respects magnetic mode. Locked layers are protected against deletion, trimming and indirect moves.

PLAYBACK
Decode prefetch now respects actual cache capacity, avoiding repeated seeks with a single-frame budget. The user reports iPhone crashes stopped; sustained performance on other devices still needs validation.

Update 2117 • 26/09/2026

URGENT EDITOR FIX
Editing panels regain usable space. The preview makes room for controls without shrinking buttons. Side tools keep their touch targets and scroll on smaller screens. Android and iOS.

SUPPORT AUREA
Optional donation invitation on app launch, with Donate and Not now choices.

Update 2116 • 26/09/2026

TIMELINE
Holding and dragging a layer keeps its options closed. Tap the layer to open its controls.

3D MODELS
Fixed reopening previously imported Android models. New imports use a persistent internal path inside the projects folder.

Update 2115 • 2026-09-26

EDITOR
Larger fill preview, circular + categories and centered selection dialogs. Preview cropping does not alter the exported project format. Timeline marker beside playback.

EFFECTS
Optical Deep Glow falloff, exposure and soft threshold. Hotspots, reverb, flanger and echo. Lens Blur, pixel ordering and manual turbulence evolution fixes. These are native implementations; exact visual parity with After Effects plugins is not verified.

PARTICLES AND CAPTIONS
Floating lights preset with a box emitter and scattered trails. Captions now open without an audio layer selected and list available sources. Generic text preset names.

VALIDATION
Sustained performance and audio still require physical iPhone and Samsung retesting.

Update 2114 • 26 September 2026

CC AND OMINO DIFFUSION
Three editable CC starting points: Detail, Cinema and Clean. Combine sharpening, contrast, exposure and saturation on an adjustment layer and save your preset. Native GPU Omino Diffusion with direction, palette, stripes and diffusion.

3D TEXT
Removed automatic wave and X/Y/Z rotation animations. Text stays still and only moves through user-authored transforms or keyframes.

PARTICLE WORLD
New 3D particle model with explosive, jet and vortex motion. Ten controls and two colors on Android and iOS. Existing projects remain readable. Based on CC Particle World; the native implementation does not reproduce its proprietary random sequence and identical visual equivalence is not established.

Update 2113 • 26 September 2026

IOS AUDIO
Fixed audio channel separation and PCM block reading. Audio still needs confirmation on a physical iPhone.

TEXT PRESETS
Eight text animations and the Preset Turbulência dinâmica preset. Parameters and expressions were extracted from the supplied files; visual equivalence with After Effects has not yet been validated.

PROJECT
New duration setting in seconds. Extending or moving a layer beyond the end also extends the project. Changing resolution fits layer framing and transform keyframes to the new canvas.

IPHONE PERFORMANCE
Use the editor speedometer to record an editing session or import a video for measurement. The stress test runs for 3 minutes. Share the report to investigate stalls and unexpected exits; validation on physical devices remains pending.

Update 2112 • 25 September 2026

UPSCALING
Android: Vulkan inference with CPU fallback when unavailable or on failure. The final 2× reduction pass uses CPU. iOS inference remains CPU-based. The model targets anime/illustration.

Temporal stabilization of static detail resets history for detected motion, cuts, fades and frame discontinuities. This is not a trained temporal model; history is limited to 64 MiB.

TIMELINE AND KEYFRAMES
Frame-aligned playhead. Panels show keys for the property being edited; dragging does not move other overlapping properties. Add/remove uses the displayed frame, and marking pauses at that frame.

EDITING AND FONTS
Fewer unnecessary UI updates. Bundled Roboto fallback no longer depends on Samsung system font files.

EXPORT AND ADS
Saved export results no longer wait for an ad callback. LevelPlay is not initialized on WebView 124.0.6367.219, the version with the reproduced media failure. This avoids the known path; it does not fix Chromium or guarantee other providers.

VALIDATION
2× and 4× GPU compared with CPU on the host; tile, cancellation, cut and motion tests. Sustained performance and fonts still require physical Samsung/iPhone acceptance.

From update 2111: themes, effect presets, touch-controlled 3D scenes, preview contrast and timeline fixes. All eight iOS gestures from that version passed on the simulator. AM import rejects detected losses; full visual equivalence remains under validation.
